claim: Since 2025-06-06 IAM requires role trust policies for recognized shared OIDC identity providers to evaluate specific JWT claims (identity-provider controls); creating or updating a role whose trust policy lacks them fails, while existing trust policies are not re-evaluated until they are modified.
question: What does IAM require since June 2025 in the trust policy of a role for a shared OIDC identity provider such as GitHub Actions?

qualifiers.scope: per role trust policy for a shared OIDC identity provider

evidence.quote: | [Identity provider controls for shared OIDC providers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_providers_oidc_secure-by-default.html) | IAM now requires explicit evaluation of specific claims in JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) for recognized shared OIDC identity providers. This security control ensures that only authorized identities from the intended organization can assume roles and access AWS resources. | June 6, 2025 |

For recognized shared OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers (IdPs), IAM requires explicit evaluation of specific claims in role trust policies. These required claims, called identity-provider controls, are evaluated by IAM during role creation and trust policy updates. If the role trust policy does not evaluate the controls required by the shared OIDC IdP, the role creation or update would fail.

Identity-provider controls will not be evaluated by IAM for existing OIDC role trust policies. For any modifications to the role trust policy for existing OIDC roles, IAM will require that identity-provider controls be included in the role trust policy.

note: FRESHNESS row 160. The list of shared providers grew on 2025-08-01 and GitHub Actions accepts job_workflow_ref since 2026-05-12 (history rows 4 and 0). Exam answer stays: restrict the trust policy with conditions on the token claims.
